name: Crimson Rampart
specific_features: The Burning Curtain -- a 200km lava wall that bisects the northern hemisphere
description: Crimson Rampart earns its name from the towering walls of solidified lava that ring its volcanic calderas in concentric formations, resembling the defensive works of some titanic siege. The surface is a hellscape of black basalt, rivers of molten rock, and sulfuric geysers that erupt with metronomic regularity. Temperatures rarely dip below scorching, and the air is a caustic blend of sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide.

From orbit, the planet glows like an ember set in the void, its lava flows tracing luminous veins across the dark crust. The Burning Curtain -- a continuous wall of slow-flowing lava stretching two hundred kilometers -- dominates the northern hemisphere, casting a permanent orange haze into the toxic sky. There is a savage, primordial beauty here, the kind that precedes all softness.

Extremophilic microorganisms thrive in the mineral-rich thermal vents, forming dense mats of heat-resistant bacteria that process sulfur compounds for energy. Early survey teams noted the uncanny regularity of the concentric lava walls, sparking debate over whether natural geological processes alone could produce such symmetry. No definitive answer has been found, but the formations continue to attract xenogeologists from across the sector.

Rich platinum deposits lie beneath the obsidian ridges, accessible only through heavily shielded mining operations. The geothermal energy potential is virtually limitless, making Crimson Rampart a prize for any faction willing to endure its punishing conditions. Several automated extraction facilities have been established and subsequently abandoned, their ruins now half-consumed by advancing lava flows.
